slug: 军事公主不会爱上魔法科学家
lines: “行了。”
奥伯伦慢条斯理地靠在椅背上，像是在看一群急于分赃却找不到门路的蠢贼，听了半天的他，最后只问了几个问题。
“阿瓦隆的那位老教皇，死了吗？”
“……据情报显示，没有，阁下。”
“阿斯特利亚的那位新上任的女王，死了吗？”
“也没有……”
“那她身边那个怪物亲王，死了吗？”
“很好。”奥伯伦弹了弹烟灰，目光扫过海图另一端那头庞大的陆地猛兽，“那么，瓦雷利亚的那群战争疯子，有趁机出兵的动作吗？”
会议室内陷入了短暂的死寂。
良久，才有人艰难地咽了口唾沫，小声回答：“……没有。”
奥伯伦面无表情地看着他们。
“既然牌桌上的巨头都没死，庄家也没掀桌子，那你们这群连底牌都凑不齐的人，跟着激动什么？”
这位唯利是图的政治家露出了狐狸般的冷笑，骨子里的那份精明在此刻展现得淋漓尽致，
“我们要做的，可不是第一个冲上去当替死鬼！”
他站起身，将燃烧的雪茄按灭在海图上阿斯特利亚的边境线上。
“通知阿尔贝里希大团长，让深潮骑士团调查一下死亡三角海域，至于其他的……继续观察。”
第七天。
圣地阿瓦隆大广场。
历史往往不会在轰鸣中翻阅篇章，而是常常沉淀于令人窒息的静谧里。
数十万信徒从清晨开始汇聚，宛如一片沉默的白色海洋。
广场四周，白色尖塔挂满黑金色挽旗，所有圣职者皆着素白祭袍。
广场中央的高台上，教皇格列高利七世缓缓走出，背脊的弧度仿佛承载着一整个时代的重量。
瑟薇娅站在高台侧后方，一同融入了这哀悼的底色，洛加里斯站在她身旁，双手拢在袖中。
奥萝拉站在教皇身后半步，低垂眼帘，璀璨的金发被纯黑的发带束起，宛如一位送葬的肃穆天使。
全场的目光如同实质般的山峦，重重压在老教皇的身上。
格列高利七世走到台前，他没有立刻说话。
沉默持续了很久，久到前排的信徒因恐惧和未知的重压而开始啜泣。
终于，老人开口。
“主的信徒们啊。”
教皇浑厚的声音，通过扩音术式，如同雷鸣般抚过整座圣山：“过去百年，神谕断绝。”
“有人说，神明抛弃了我们。”
“有人说，圣光已经远离人间，也有人因此迷惘，痛苦，在深夜里怀疑自己一生所信，是否只是一场宏大的虚妄。”
他停顿了一下，枯瘦的手掌按在胸前冰冷的圣徽上。
“今日，我以圣教廷现任教皇之名，向世人宣告这百年长夜的真相。”

"Okay."
Oberon leaned back in his chair slowly, as if looking at a group of stupid thieves who were eager to share their loot but couldn't find a way out. He listened for a long time and finally only asked a few questions.
"Is the old pope of Avalon dead?"
"...according to intelligence, no, Your Excellency."
"Is the new queen of Astraea dead?"
"No..."
"Then the monster prince next to her is dead?"
"...Nothing either."
"Very good." Oberon flicked the ashes of his cigarette and glanced at the huge land beast on the other side of the chart. "So, are those war madmen in Valyria taking the opportunity to send troops?"
There was a brief silence in the conference room.
After a long time, someone swallowed hard and replied in a low voice: "...No."
Oberyn looked at them expressionlessly.
"Since the giants at the card table are not dead, and the dealer has not lifted the table, then why are you people who can't even collect the hole cards, why are you so excited?"
This profit-seeking politician showed a fox-like sneer, and the shrewdness in his bones was clearly displayed at this moment.
"What we have to do is not be the first to rush forward and be the scapegoat!"
He stood up and put out the burning cigar on the border of Astralia on the sea chart.
"Inform Grand Commander Alberich and let the Knights of the Deep Tide investigate the Triangle of Death. As for the rest...continue to observe."
…
The seventh day.
The main square of Avalon in the Holy Land.
History often does not turn its pages in a roar, but often settles in suffocating silence.
Hundreds of thousands of believers have gathered since early morning, like a silent white ocean.
Around the square, white minarets are hung with black and gold flags, and all clergymen wear plain white robes.
On the high platform in the center of the square, Pope Gregory VII slowly walked out, the arc of his back seeming to carry the weight of an entire era.
Serviya stood behind the high platform and blended into the background of mourning. Logaris stood beside her with his hands in his sleeves.
Aurora stood half a step behind the Pope, her eyes lowered, her bright blond hair tied up by a pure black hairband, like a solemn angel in mourning.
The gazes of the entire audience were like solid mountains, pressing heavily on the old pope.
Gregory VII came to the stage, but he did not speak immediately.
The silence lasted for so long that the believers in the front row began to sob from the weight of fear and the unknown.
Finally, the old man spoke.
"O followers of the Lord."
The pope's rich voice, through the amplification technique, caressed the entire holy mountain like thunder: "In the past hundred years, the oracle has been cut off."
"Some say the gods have abandoned us."
"Some people say that the Holy Light has left the world, and some people are confused and painful because of it, and wonder in the middle of the night whether what they believe in their whole lives is just a grand illusion."
He paused and pressed his skinny palms on the cold holy symbol on his chest.
"Today, in the name of the current Pope of the Holy See, I declare to the world the truth of this hundred-year night."
